lines.text: Skin and hair are defining features of our physical appearance. Skin can be described by its complexion — fair, olive, dark, or tanned — and by its condition: smooth, rough, dry, or oily. Freckles, moles, and birthmarks add unique character to each face. Skin care is a global industry, with products for cleansing, moisturizing, and protecting against sun damage. Wrinkles and fine lines naturally appear with age, though sunscreen helps prevent premature aging. Hair varies enormously across individuals. It can be straight, wavy, curly, or coily. Hair texture ranges from fine and silky to thick and coarse. Natural hair color includes shades of blonde, brunette, auburn, red, and black, though many people dye their hair for a fresh look. Hairstyles are both personal expression and cultural identity — from a simple ponytail or braid to an elaborate updo or a clean buzz cut. Facial hair on men includes beards, moustaches, sideburns, and stubble. Hair loss — thinning, receding hairlines, and baldness — affects many adults. Understanding this vocabulary helps describe people accurately and discuss grooming, beauty routines, and personal style with confidence.
